plan.title: bug(agents-md): resolveFrameworkSha runs git in the framework install root — spurious git fatal AND sha=unknown persisted into consumer AGENTS.md (#3914 / #4118 still reproduce at 0.104.0)

narratives.Description: bug(agents-md): resolveFrameworkSha runs git in the framework install root — spurious git fatal AND sha=unknown persisted into consumer AGENTS.md (#3914 / #4118 still reproduce at 0.104.0)
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

#3914 ("Align read-only syntax and suppress spurious Git fatal output") and #4118 ("session:start prints git fatal twice then succeeds on an npm deposit") are both closed, but **both symptoms still reproduce at 0.104.0** — and there is a third, worse symptom from the same root cause that neither issue mentions: the bad value gets **persisted into the consumer's tracked `AGENTS.md`**.

Filing fresh rather than commenting on closed issues, per the pattern in #3511.

## Root cause

`dist/platform/agents-md.js:52`:

```js
function resolveFrameworkSha(seams = {}) {
    if (seams.resolveSha) return seams.resolveSha();
    const root = frameworkRoot(seams);
    try {
        const stdout = execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "--short=12", "HEAD"], {
            cwd: root, encoding: "utf8", timeout: 5000,
        });
        const sha = stdout.trim();
        return sha || "unknown";
    } catch {
        return "unknown";
    }
}
```

`cwd` is the **framework's own install root**. On a global/npm install that is `<prefix>/lib/node_modules/@deftai/directive/...`, which is not a git repository — exactly the "npm deposit" case #4118 named. So git writes `fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git` to stderr, `execFileSync` throws, the catch returns `"unknown"`, and that string is written into the managed-section marker.

One cause, three symptoms.

## Symptom 1 — spurious git fatal (was #4118 / #3914)

Isolated to `agents:refresh`; other verbs are clean:

```
deft doctor                     -> git-fatal lines: 0
deft agents:refresh             -> git-fatal lines: 1
deft verify:vbrief-conformance  -> git-fatal lines: 0
deft triage:queue               -> git-fatal lines: 0
```

`session:start` prints it too, because orientation runs `agents_refresh`. From a directory where `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolves the consumer repo perfectly — the failure is entirely about the `cwd` handed to git.

## Symptom 2 — `sha=unknown` persisted into consumer `AGENTS.md` (unreported)

This is the part worth fixing beyond cosmetics. `agents:refresh` stamps:

```
<!-- deft:managed-section v3 sha=unknown refreshed=2026-09-05T22:11:14Z session=143c8023a0a8 -->
```

Before the refresh, the same repo carried a real hash (`sha=089bbf450e1a`). So a global-install `agents:refresh` **downgrades** a good marker to `unknown`, in a tracked file, which then gets committed. Downstream, `session:start` reports `managed=current sha=unknown` and drift detection has no content hash to compare against — it is comparing to a sentinel forever.

A second `agents:refresh` then reports `unchanged - sha match`, so the degraded state is self-consistent and gives no hint anything is wrong.

## Symptom 3 — read-only syntax still misdocumented (was #3914)

The CLI rejects the documented form:

```
$ deft session:start -- --read-only
session_start: unrecognized argument: --

$ deft session:start --read-only
[deft] read-only session posture (alignment only; no ritual-state write)   # works
```

And the shipped 0.104.0 docs still instruct the broken form — including the **managed** AGENTS.md section the framework writes into consumer repos:

- `.deft/core/commands.md:377` — ``? Explicit read-only alignment only: `deft session:start -- --read-only` (no ritual-state write).``
- managed `AGENTS.md:42` — ``? `deft session:start -- --read-only` (#2176).``

An agent following the managed constitution literally hits an error on the first read-only orientation of every session. (The `--` is Taskfile passthrough syntax; it is wrong when invoking `deft` directly, so the docs are conflating the two entrypoints.)

## Suggested fix

For symptoms 1 and 2, `resolveFrameworkSha` should not shell out to git against its own install root. Options:

1. **Read the version/sha from the deposit's own metadata** rather than git — `.deft/GENERATION.json` already carries `contentVersion` and per-surface versions, and the package carries its `package.json` version. A source install can still prefer git.
2. **Detect a git work tree before invoking git** (`git rev-parse --git-dir` guarded, or check for `.git`), and skip silently when absent.
3. At minimum, pass `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "ignore"]` so the fatal never reaches the user's terminal — but that only hides symptom 1 and leaves `sha=unknown` being written, which is the damaging half.
4. **Never downgrade an existing marker.** If a sha cannot be resolved, preserve the marker's current sha rather than overwriting it with `unknown`.

(1) plus (4) together fix all of it: real value where resolvable, no regression where not.

For symptom 3, correct both doc surfaces to `deft session:start --read-only`, keeping the `--` form only where a `task` invocation is shown.

## Environment

`@deftai/directive` 0.104.0 (engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.104.0`), global install at `~/.local/lib/node_modules` (npm prefix `~/.local`), vendored deposit v0.104.0, macOS 25.5, Node 22.23.2, git 2.50.1.

## Gate stamp

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-11T17:13:34Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

Pin: d8f4e2a0f8be478096385ec0b765d313e6d4e110. Ceiling 5637953229 inclusive. Open critique, N=1, round 1. This session did not run a global npm `agents:refresh`.

## 1. Preserve-existing-sha cannot bind on write paths

class: blocks-the-design

Evidence: `agentsRefreshPlan` (`packages/core/src/platform/agents-md.ts`) calls `resolveSha()` then `attributeRenderManagedSection` on every plan. Writable states are only `absent` / `missing` / `stale` (`AGENTS_REFRESH_WRITABLE_STATES`). When stripped body equals the template, state is `current` and `new_content` is the existing file, so the marker `sha=` is already kept. `resolveFrameworkSha` returns `"unknown"` when `payloadIsOwnGitRoot` is false. The issue's recommended pair is option 1 plus option 4 ("never downgrade an existing marker").

Failure mode: option 4 only has work on a write. That write is a template-body change (or first insert). Preserving a prior checkout short-SHA (example in the issue: `sha=089bbf450e1a`) onto bytes that came from an npm deposit labels the new constitution with a git identity it did not come from. `probeManagedSectionDrift` then reports that embedded `sha=` on `managed=current`. A tracked consumer `AGENTS.md` carries a false provenance stamp.

Disposition: a successor lean cannot bind option 4 as a write-path preserve. Current-state already preserves. Remaining write paths need a resolvable identity (option 1 against inventory below), not a leftover git SHA.

## 2. Git-fatal / detect-then-skip / stdio-ignore are not the remaining hole

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: `resolveFrameworkSha` returns `"unknown"` before `timedGitRunner` when `payloadIsOwnGitRoot(root)` is false. `payloadIsOwnGitRoot` uses `timedGitRunner(10_000)` `rev-parse --show-toplevel` and compares resolved toplevel to the payload dir (`packages/core/src/platform/resolve-version.ts`). `execGit` uses `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` (`packages/core/src/session/git.ts`). Tests lock silence and `"unknown"`: `packages/core/src/platform/branch-coverage.test.ts` "silent git probes on non-git payload roots (#4118)"; `packages/cli/src/session-start.test.ts` "framework SHA own-git-root (#3914)". CHANGELOG at this pin records #4118 swallow and #3914 own-git-root. Issue body still shows the pre-guard `execFileSync` snippet.

Failure mode: binding options 2 and 3, or treating stderr `fatal: not a git repository` as still open, recuts #3914 / #4118. Implementers re-silence a probe the tests already lock silent.

Disposition: drop options 2 and 3 from the remaining set. Keep the unknown stamp (finding 1's write path, finding 3's reporting) and the docs split (finding 4).

## 3. "unchanged - sha match" is content-current phrasing, not marker-sha equality

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: `runAgentsRefresh` prints `formatDepositShaMatchLine("agents:refresh")` when `state === "current"` (`packages/cli/src/agents-refresh.ts`). The file comment says content-based; deposit fingerprint alone is not the plan. `computeDepositSha` hashes engine + payload version + templates (`packages/core/src/session/deposit-sha.ts`) and is a different 12-hex. `probeManagedSectionDrift` already records `embeddedSha` plus `bodyHash` (SHA-256-12 of stripped body). Production `plan()` calls `reconcileVersions` without `expectedManagedSectionSha` (`packages/core/src/resolution/plan.ts` `contentStale`). `contentStale` treats `managedSectionSha === null` as stale; the string `"unknown"` is not null. Session-start `managed=current sha=` prints the embedded marker (`formatHostContentSurfaceLines`).

Failure mode: binding "drift detection compares to a sentinel forever" and "second refresh sha-match hides the damage" as one detector. The second refresh is a content no-op. The damage is the first stale/absent/missing write of `sha=unknown`, plus host-surface echoing that embedded value.

Disposition: bind the unknown write on writable states. Do not bind a live expected-vs-embedded SHA gate this pin does not run. Do not treat `computeDepositSha` as already filling `sha=` (it is not wired there).

## 4. Read-only docs: commands.md is split; CLI accepts `-- --`; agents-entry keep is locked

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: `content/commands.md` (session-start ritual): `deft session:start --read-only` and `task session:start -- --read-only`; it does not contain `deft session:start -- --read-only`. `parseArgs` skips a lone `--` (`packages/cli/src/session-start.test.ts` `#3914`). `content/templates/agents-entry.md` Session routing still has `deft session:start -- --read-only`. `packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/agents_md_session_start.test.ts` requires that exact string in agents-entry and requires the split in commands.md. CHANGELOG #3914 records keeping `-- --` on the managed agents-entry line. Consumer template forbids bare `task session:start` (`CONSUMER_FORBIDDEN_BARE_TASK_MARKERS`). The issue's 0.104.0 repro `unrecognized argument: --` is not this pin's parser.

Failure mode: "correct both doc surfaces" plus "CLI still rejects" recuts a closed commands.md split, fights the #3914 keep, and goes red on `agents_md_session_start.test.ts` if the template changes without the lock test.

Disposition: do not bind CLI reject or a commands.md recut. If the consumer line should match `deft session:start --read-only`, the bound remedy is agents-entry plus that content-contract test, as a deliberate recut of the #3914 keep, not leftover 0.104.0 docs.

## Injection / swarm

The stamp is written into consumer-tracked `AGENTS.md` (shared constitution, identity, authority). Preserve-wrong-sha (finding 1) is an identity lie in that file, not a log-line cosmetic. Stamping a second git-shaped 12-hex next to existing `computeDepositSha` / `bodyHash` collides two "sha" namespaces unless `sha=` is redefined. Untrusted input here is the consumer tree plus the install root; the fail-closed risk is false provenance, not a bypass. Do not skip `payloadIsOwnGitRoot` (it still blocks stamping an enclosing repo SHA from a nested non-checkout).

## Inventory (existing, not new)

- `resolveFrameworkSha`: seam or `payloadIsOwnGitRoot` else `"unknown"`; `timedGitRunner(5000)` `rev-parse --short=12 HEAD` only on own git root.
- `payloadIsOwnGitRoot`: silent git runner; false when toplevel missing or not equal to the payload dir. Tests lock silent + false.
- `agentsRefreshPlan`: always stamps `frameworkSha` into attributed output; `current` keeps existing bytes; writable states write that sha, including `"unknown"`. No preserve-existing-sha branch.
- `.deft/GENERATION.json`: `contentVersion`, monotonic `generation`, surface fingerprints (`readLiveGeneration` / `stampLiveGeneration`).
- `package.json` version: `readCorePackageVersion` (`@deftai/directive-core`).
- `computeDepositSha`: engine + payload version (prefers live generation) + templates hash. Used for orientation no-op phrasing, not `sha=`.
- `probeManagedSectionDrift.bodyHash`: content identity of the managed body, already reported beside embedded sha.
- `resolveVersion`: ENV / VERSION / `.deft-version` / git describe (git path also own-git-root gated).
- Docs: commands.md already splits deft vs task; agents-entry still `deft session:start -- --read-only`; `agents_md_session_start.test.ts` locks both.

## Road not taken

- Option 2 (detect work tree, skip git): already the `payloadIsOwnGitRoot` guard. Rejected as remaining work.
- Option 3 (stdio ignore only): already `timedGitRunner` capture. Rejected; it would leave `"unknown"` writes, which the issue itself names as the damaging half.
- Option 4 write-path preserve: rejected (finding 1).
- Mint a new git-shaped 12-hex from templates only: rejected while `bodyHash` and `computeDepositSha` already exist.

## Steelman

Strongest salvage of option 4: last-known-good SHA in a tracked marker is better than the literal `unknown`, and `refreshed=` already records the write time, so `sha=` could mean "last resolved framework identity" rather than "identity of these bytes."

What would flip finding 1: an explicit redefinition that `sha=` is a cache of the last successful git resolve and is allowed to outlive the template body, with drift using `bodyHash` / deposit version instead. The attribute sits next to `refreshed=` and `session=` on the write that just rendered the section. This pin does not record that redefinition.

What would flip finding 4: `parseArgs` again treating a lone `--` as an unrecognized argument, or commands.md still showing `deft session:start -- --read-only`. Neither is true at this SHA.

## Footnote

class: footnote

`resolveFrameworkSha` is not exported; tests go through `agentsRefreshPlan`. Doctor `agents-md.ts` re-exports the same plan. No second SHA probe found under `scripts/`.

## In plain English

Git-fatal on npm deposits is already silent. agents:refresh still stamps sha=unknown on writable states. Preserving a leftover checkout SHA onto new npm bytes is a false provenance stamp. commands.md already splits deft vs task; agents-entry still has deft session:start -- --read-only because a #3914 test keeps it.

If this map is confirmed, the next-build is a resolvable identity on write (inventory: generation / package version / deposit fingerprint / bodyHash), not preserve-existing-sha, not re-silence git. Docs: only recut agents-entry plus its lock test if the consumer line should match deft --read-only.

## Bound remedy

- Drop options 2, 3, and write-path preserve (4). Remaining hole is writable states (absent/missing/stale) stamping sha=unknown. Supply a resolvable identity from existing inventory (GENERATION.json / package version / computeDepositSha / bodyHash). Do not preserve a leftover git short-SHA onto npm-rendered bytes. Do not mint a second git-shaped 12-hex next to those hashes without redefining sha=.
- Keep payloadIsOwnGitRoot. Do not reopen #3914 / #4118 as git-fatal.
- Do not bind a live expected-vs-embedded SHA gate this pin does not run. Bind the unknown write.
- Do not recut commands.md or claim CLI still rejects -- --. If the consumer line should be deft session:start --read-only, recut agents-entry plus agents_md_session_start.test.ts as a deliberate recut of the #3914 keep. CHANGELOG.
